title: German director Wenders clarifies views on film and politics
gist: German director Wim Wenders walked back the perception left by his February Berlin film festival remarks that filmmakers 'cannot really enter the field of politics,' clarifying at Venice that filmmakers are the empathetic 'antidote' to politicians rather than apolitical, as the Gaza war continues to be a recurring flashpoint at European film festivals.

insights.claim: Wim Wenders, while heading the Berlin film festival jury in February 2026, told reporters filmmakers 'cannot really enter the field of politics' when asked about Germany's support for Israel during the Gaza war — a remark that sparked controversy and which he now says was misunderstood.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The controversy shows how any public remark on Gaza by a prominent cultural figure, however nuanced, can spiral into a reputational flashpoint requiring later clarification — relevant to reputational-risk monitoring around cultural/entertainment figures tied to Gaza commentary.
insights.quote: Wenders told reporters that filmmakers "cannot really enter the field of politics" when he was asked about Germany's support for Israel throughout the Gaza war.

insights.claim: Wenders clarified in Venice that his actual view is the opposite of apolitical detachment: filmmakers operate with empathy, unlike politicians, and are therefore 'the antidote' to politics rather than separate from it.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The clarification reframes the artist's stance from 'stay out of politics' to 'actively counter politics through empathy,' a distinction relevant to how cultural institutions position themselves on contested geopolitical issues.
insights.quote: "We are not working with a mindset of politicians, we are working with a mindset of empathetic people. And we are into changing things... we have to stay out of politics because we do the opposite. We are the antidote," he added.

insights.claim: Venice Film Festival jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal countered at the festival's opening press conference that movies are 'fundamentally, undeniably political,' a more explicit stance than Wenders' framing.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Divergent public positions among top festival figures (Wenders' 'empathy vs. politics' framing versus Gyllenhaal's blunt 'undeniably political') illustrate an unresolved industry-wide tension likely to keep resurfacing at future festivals tied to Gaza commentary.
insights.quote: jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal weighed in on the topic, saying that movies are "fundamentally, undeniably political".

insights.claim: The Gaza war has become a recurring political flashpoint at European film festivals, with organizers and industry figures repeatedly pressed for their views on the conflict.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The pattern of Gaza-related controversies recurring at festival after festival signals sustained reputational and programming risk for cultural events and their sponsors as the conflict continues.
insights.quote: The war in Gaza has been a frequent political flashpoint at European film festivals, with organisers and movie industry leading lights asked for their views on the conflict.
